In French, l’arracheur-de-nerfs – literally tongue-surgeon – has been used as an insult since the Late 18 ^{th} century.
An arracheur-de-dents (arracheur de dents) was a French dentist who removed tooth roots by cutting away the tissue around the tooth. The name was derived from their practice of splitting the jaw in two before amputating both jaws, thus breaking both pieces apart and allowing each side to heal separately without further complication.
There exists also another French expression, l’homme mient encore son coup ou l’homme qui mente toujours (a true Frenchmen always keeps lying), which shows how common it has become during the past century or more.
